k: You found me! Up here you can see the whole sky. It's mostly purple.
src: 'You found me! Up here you can see the whole sky. It\'s mostly purple.'

k: I like it. Don't tell Mum, she thinks purple's sad.
src: 'I like it. Don\'t tell Mum, she thinks purple\'s sad.'

k: I was _guarding_ the skiff. Undercover. You blew my cover.
src: 'I was _guarding_ the skiff. Undercover. You blew my cover.'

k: Fine. I'll go tell Tansy. She's going to be so smug.
src: 'Fine. I\'ll go tell Tansy. She\'s going to be so smug.'

k: Shhh! The Baron's terrace is the best spot. Nobody looks at the Baron's stuff. It's all ugly.
src: 'Shhh! The Baron\'s terrace is the best spot. Nobody looks at the Baron\'s stuff. It\'s all ugly.'

k: Nobody finds Sprocket. I'm Sprocket. _Nobody finds me._
src: 'Nobody finds Sprocket. I\'m Sprocket. _Nobody finds me._'

k: I need a new spot. I need to think about my life.
src: 'I need a new spot. I need to think about my life.'

k: The old signal mast. Someone has carved every Kite's name into it, from the bottom up. The top name is PIP. Under it, smaller, somebody else has carved: BOSS.
src: 'The old signal mast. Someone has carved every Kite\'s name into it, from the bottom up. The top name is PIP. Under it, smaller, somebody else has carved: BOSS.'

k: The town kite-pole. A hundred kite-tails flap from it, one for every child the shard has lost to the wind or the raiders. They snap in the gusts like applause.
src: 'The town kite-pole. A hundred kite-tails flap from it, one for every child the shard has lost to the wind or the raiders. They snap in the gusts like applause.'

k: The end of the dock. Below: nothing, then haze, then more nothing. The wind tugs at your coat like it has somewhere to show you.
src: 'The end of the dock. Below: nothing, then haze, then more nothing. The wind tugs at your coat like it has somewhere to show you.'

k: The ladder down to the Underhang. The Kites have chalked a warning on the top rung: DONT. (BOSS SAYS.)
src: 'The ladder down to the Underhang. The Kites have chalked a warning on the top rung: DONT. (BOSS SAYS.)'

k: Kestrel's tab is closed, by the way. He came in, paid what he had, and ordered a water. A _water_. I nearly called Ilse.
src: 'Kestrel\'s tab is closed, by the way. He came in, paid what he had, and ordered a water. A _water_. I nearly called Ilse.'

k: Bed's a hammock, roof's a sail, breakfast is whatever the wind brings. Hundred and fifty.
src: 'Bed\'s a hammock, roof\'s a sail, breakfast is whatever the wind brings. Hundred and fifty.'

k: the Rusty Anchor
src: 'the Rusty Anchor'

k: Your big friend loses every hand. Every one. I used to think he was the worst card player alive.
src: 'Your big friend loses every hand. Every one. I used to think he was the worst card player alive.'

k: Then I noticed he only loses when there's a Kite watching. Kites get the pot. Every time.
src: 'Then I noticed he only loses when there\'s a Kite watching. Kites get the pot. Every time.'

k: The Baron banned singing after the raiders' lullabies started drifting up from below.
src: 'The Baron banned singing after the raiders\' lullabies started drifting up from below.'

k: So now I hum. Very quietly. Hmmmm. That one's about a sailor.
src: 'So now I hum. Very quietly. Hmmmm. That one\'s about a sailor.'

k: They say Evernoon is a city where it's always summer. They say the dead walk around in it, happy.
src: 'They say Evernoon is a city where it\'s always summer. They say the dead walk around in it, happy.'

k: My wife's dead. I don't want her happy somewhere I can't go. That's selfish, isn't it. I'm drinking about it.
src: 'My wife\'s dead. I don\'t want her happy somewhere I can\'t go. That\'s selfish, isn\'t it. I\'m drinking about it.'

k: A hammock with a blanket folded very neatly at the foot. A greatsword leans beside it. Scratched on the wall above, a tally of days — and beside every seventh mark, a tiny drawing of a shield.
src: 'A hammock with a blanket folded very neatly at the foot. A greatsword leans beside it. Scratched on the wall above, a tally of days — and beside every seventh mark, a tiny drawing of a shield.'

k: I cried when I woke up. I always cry when I wake up. Boss says it's because I'm surprised to be alive.
src: 'I cried when I woke up. I always cry when I wake up. Boss says it\'s because I\'m surprised to be alive.'

k: I think it's because waking up is sad. Even when it's good.
src: 'I think it\'s because waking up is sad. Even when it\'s good.'

k: Bram swung his sword so hard the Baron's gun fell off the roof. Probably. I wasn't looking. I was hiding. Hiding's a job.
src: 'Bram swung his sword so hard the Baron\'s gun fell off the roof. Probably. I wasn\'t looking. I was hiding. Hiding\'s a job.'

k: Rule nine: no grown-ups in the Nest.
src: 'Rule nine: no grown-ups in the Nest.'

k: ...You're the Boss's friends? Rule nine-and-a-half: unless they're the Boss's friends. I just made that up. It's allowed.
src: '...You\'re the Boss\'s friends? Rule nine-and-a-half: unless they\'re the Boss\'s friends. I just made that up. It\'s allowed.'

k: I'm building my own kite. It's a dragon. Well. It's a triangle. It's a dragon on the inside.
src: 'I\'m building my own kite. It\'s a dragon. Well. It\'s a triangle. It\'s a dragon on the inside.'

k: A map of Kiteholm drawn on a sail, covered in pins and string. Every Kite has a pin. Every pin has a name. In the corner, a list in a careful child's hand: FOOD. WATER. SLINGSHOTS. COUNT HEADS. COUNT AGAIN.
src: 'A map of Kiteholm drawn on a sail, covered in pins and string. Every Kite has a pin. Every pin has a name. In the corner, a list in a careful child\'s hand: FOOD. WATER. SLINGSHOTS. COUNT HEADS. COUNT AGAIN.'

k: Tucked under the map's corner: a folded scrap of paper. Inside, in pencil, a drawing of four tall people and two short ones on a beach. One of the tall ones has a sword. One of the short ones is holding her hand.
src: 'Tucked under the map\'s corner: a folded scrap of paper. Inside, in pencil, a drawing of four tall people and two short ones on a beach. One of the tall ones has a sword. One of the short ones is holding her hand.'

k: The Baron's statue is of the Baron. By the Baron. He posed for eleven days.
src: 'The Baron\'s statue is of the Baron. By the Baron. He posed for eleven days.'

k: He says it captures his "essence." Its essence is mostly chin.
src: 'He says it captures his "essence." Its essence is mostly chin.'

k: A statue of Baron Dask, welded from scrap, gazing nobly at nothing. A plaque reads: "THE AIR IS FREE. BREATHING IT IS NOT."
src: 'A statue of Baron Dask, welded from scrap, gazing nobly at nothing. A plaque reads: "THE AIR IS FREE. BREATHING IT IS NOT."'

k: Crates of salvage stamped with the Choir's sunburst. The Baron does business with everyone. Everyone does business with the Baron. That is what makes him a Baron.
src: 'Crates of salvage stamped with the Choir\'s sunburst. The Baron does business with everyone. Everyone does business with the Baron. That is what makes him a Baron.'

k: Arena
src: 'Arena'

k: I bet on the Gale Roc every week. The Gale Roc has never lost.
src: 'I bet on the Gale Roc every week. The Gale Roc has never lost.'

k: I am very rich and very sad.
src: 'I am very rich and very sad.'

k: Iron Moll used to be a Dawnguard sergeant. Now she fights scrap for scrap.
src: 'Iron Moll used to be a Dawnguard sergeant. Now she fights scrap for scrap.'

k: She says it's the same job with better hours.
src: 'She says it\'s the same job with better hours.'

k: Chalked rankings: RUSTJAW. COG & SPROCKET (THE TWINS, NOT THE KITE). IRON MOLL. THE GALE ROC — UNDEFEATED. Underneath, someone has added: THE BARON (IN HIS DREAMS).
src: 'Chalked rankings: RUSTJAW. COG & SPROCKET (THE TWINS, NOT THE KITE). IRON MOLL. THE GALE ROC — UNDEFEATED. Underneath, someone has added: THE BARON (IN HIS DREAMS).'

k: Satchel
src: 'Satchel'

k: Nest
src: 'Nest'

k: A rope bridge that used to go straight down to the lower shelf. The ropes have been cut — cleanly. Someone did not want company.
src: 'A rope bridge that used to go straight down to the lower shelf. The ropes have been cut — cleanly. Someone did not want company.'

k: A kite-tail snagged on the rocks, faded almost white. Somebody's, once.
src: 'A kite-tail snagged on the rocks, faded almost white. Somebody\'s, once.'

k: The split prow of a Choir galleon, driven into the rock like a nail. Gilt letters on the hull, half burned away: _VIGIL_.
src: 'The split prow of a Choir galleon, driven into the rock like a nail. Gilt letters on the hull, half burned away: _VIGIL_.'

k: Wick is asleep, smiling. "...five more minutes..."
src: 'Wick is asleep, smiling. "...five more minutes..."'

k: Moth is asleep. Her lips move: "...so many candles..."
src: 'Moth is asleep. Her lips move: "...so many candles..."'

k: A child from another shard. You don't know her name. In her sleep she is holding a hand that isn't there.
src: 'A child from another shard. You don\'t know her name. In her sleep she is holding a hand that isn\'t there.'

k: Desk
src: 'Desk'

k: Brig door
src: 'Brig door'

k: A breach in the hull. Through it: the underside of the world, and wind, and a long way down.
src: 'A breach in the hull. Through it: the underside of the world, and wind, and a long way down.'

k: The captain's shelf. Hymnals, a logbook, and a child's drawing of the sun, pinned up carefully. The sun has a face. It is smiling. It is not moving.
src: 'The captain\'s shelf. Hymnals, a logbook, and a child\'s drawing of the sun, pinned up carefully. The sun has a face. It is smiling. It is not moving.'

k: Gloam crystals grown through the deck like teeth. They hum in the same key as the lullaby.
src: 'Gloam crystals grown through the deck like teeth. They hum in the same key as the lullaby.'

k: The lullaby swells, sweet and endless, from the bow. Somewhere in this ship, children are sleeping. Find them first.
src: 'The lullaby swells, sweet and endless, from the bow. Somewhere in this ship, children are sleeping. Find them first.'

k: The Marigold. A sky-ferry. Forty seats, still bolted in, all facing the windows.
src: 'The Marigold. A sky-ferry. Forty seats, still bolted in, all facing the windows.'

k: On one seat, a paper bag of sweets, unopened. Someone was saving them for the view.
src: 'On one seat, a paper bag of sweets, unopened. Someone was saving them for the view.'

k: You climb the crane-tower. From the top, the Boneyard is a river of broken ships, running all the way down the canyon to the dark.
src: 'You climb the crane-tower. From the top, the Boneyard is a river of broken ships, running all the way down the canyon to the dark.'

k: Far to the north-east, three bright shards hang in a slanting line, as if someone had thrown them and they never landed.
src: 'Far to the north-east, three bright shards hang in a slanting line, as if someone had thrown them and they never landed.'

k: Strongbox
src: 'Strongbox'

k: The strongbox lies open and quiet. Whatever it was, it is only a box now.
src: 'The strongbox lies open and quiet. Whatever it was, it is only a box now.'

k: A gilded strongbox, half-buried beside the upturned hull of the Gilded Gull. The lock is shaped like a smile.
src: 'A gilded strongbox, half-buried beside the upturned hull of the Gilded Gull. The lock is shaped like a smile.'

k: Pry it open?
src: 'Pry it open?'

k: The smile gets wider.
src: 'The smile gets wider.'

k: The Gilded Gull, lying on her back like a beetle. Her lift-coil housing is empty, torn open from the inside.
src: 'The Gilded Gull, lying on her back like a beetle. Her lift-coil housing is empty, torn open from the inside.'

k: Censer
src: 'Censer'

k: Luggage, still strapped to the rail. A name-tag: TILDE, AGED 9, TO AURENNE. PLEASE RETURN IF LOST.
src: 'Luggage, still strapped to the rail. A name-tag: TILDE, AGED 9, TO AURENNE. PLEASE RETURN IF LOST.'

k: Nobody did.
src: 'Nobody did.'
